notes: All expected answers were computed directly against source.sqlite with the reference SQL shown.
reference_date is the value of 'now' assumed by every question; the agent must be configurable to use it.
Timestamps are compared as UTC epoch seconds. Window boundaries are inclusive of the start day and exclusive of the end day.
Currency conversion uses rate_cards.fx_rate (one constant per currency: USD 1.0, EUR 1.08, GBP 1.27, BRL 0.19) as a multiplier into USD, the reporting currency.
For list answers, scoring is set-based on the key field unless 'ordered' is true. Numeric fields are scored with the tolerance given on the question.
A 'reference_sql' is one correct way to get the answer, not the only one.

questions.question: Who in EMEA has Python at proficiency 4 or higher and is less than 60% hard-booked between March and May 2026?

parameters.capacity_note: 65 working days x 8 h; any reasonable capacity assumption is acceptable because every candidate is far below 60%

questions.reference_sql:
WITH cand AS (
  SELECT p.person_id, p.display_name, ps.proficiency
  FROM people p JOIN person_skills ps ON ps.person_id = p.person_id
  WHERE p.location_region = 'EMEA'
    AND ps.skill_id = (SELECT skill_id FROM skills WHERE name = 'Python')
    AND ps.proficiency >= 4),
hard AS (
  SELECT person_id, SUM(minutes) / 60.0 AS hours
  FROM bookings
  WHERE kind = 'hard' AND start_ts < :window_end AND end_ts >= :window_start
  GROUP BY person_id)
SELECT c.display_name, c.proficiency, ROUND(COALESCE(h.hours, 0), 1) AS hard_booked_hours
FROM cand c LEFT JOIN hard h ON h.person_id = c.person_id
ORDER BY hard_booked_hours, c.display_name;

questions.question: Which open resource requirements belong to engagements with a critical risk and still have no submitted request?

scoring.partial_credit: count within 2 of 32 with no false positives scores 0.5

pitfalls: 'open' means status_lookup.state_group = 'open' for domain 'requirement' (codes OPN and PRT), not only code OPN
resource_requirements.request_status is a denormalised text column; the question is about requirement_requests.state
questions.reference_sql:
SELECT rr.requirement_id, rr.name, en.code
FROM resource_requirements rr
JOIN status_lookup sl ON sl.status_id = rr.status_id AND sl.domain = 'requirement' AND sl.state_group = 'open'
JOIN engagements en ON en.engagement_id = rr.engagement_id
WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM risks k WHERE k.engagement_id = en.engagement_id AND k.severity = 'critical')
  AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM requirement_requests rq WHERE rq.requirement_id = rr.requirement_id AND rq.state = 'submitted')
ORDER BY rr.requirement_id;

questions.question: What is the total planned cost, in the reporting currency, of active engagements in the Healthcare & Life Sciences business unit?
pitfalls: Three currencies are involved; summing the unconverted amounts gives 4,791,135.52, which is wrong
'active' is status_lookup code ACT in domain 'project'
questions.reference_sql:
SELECT en.code, cur.iso_code, en.planned_cost_cents / 100.0 AS planned_cost,
       en.planned_cost_cents / 100.0 * fx.fx_rate AS planned_cost_usd
FROM engagements en
JOIN status_lookup sl ON sl.status_id = en.status_id AND sl.domain = 'project' AND sl.code = 'ACT'
JOIN business_units bu ON bu.business_unit_id = en.business_unit_id AND bu.code = 'HLS'
JOIN currencies cur ON cur.currency_id = en.currency_id
JOIN (SELECT currency_id, MAX(fx_rate) AS fx_rate FROM rate_cards GROUP BY currency_id) fx ON fx.currency_id = en.currency_id;

questions.question: How many people in each region have the DSPy / LLM Ops skill at proficiency 3 or higher?

scoring.note: Reporting APAC as 0 or omitting it are both acceptable

questions.reference_sql:
SELECT p.location_region, COUNT(*) AS people
FROM people p
JOIN person_skills ps ON ps.person_id = p.person_id
JOIN skills s ON s.skill_id = ps.skill_id
WHERE s.name = 'DSPy / LLM Ops' AND ps.proficiency >= 3
GROUP BY p.location_region ORDER BY p.location_region;

questions.question: Who logged the most hours on ENG-2026-0001 in the first quarter of 2026, and how many hours were logged on it in total that quarter?
pitfalls: time entries join to engagements through work_items
questions.reference_sql:
SELECT p.display_name, SUM(te.minutes) / 60.0 AS hours
FROM time_entries te
JOIN work_items wi ON wi.work_item_id = te.work_item_id
JOIN engagements en ON en.engagement_id = wi.engagement_id
JOIN people p ON p.person_id = te.person_id
WHERE en.code = 'ENG-2026-0001' AND te.entry_ts >= :q1_start AND te.entry_ts < :q2_start
GROUP BY p.person_id ORDER BY hours DESC LIMIT 5;

questions.question: How many critical-path work items are currently blocked on active engagements, and which engagements have the most?

expected.top_note: Five engagements are tied at 2 blocked items; any of them are acceptable as 'the most'

pitfalls: Two different status domains are involved: 'task' for the work item (BLK) and 'project' for the engagement (ACT)
is_critical is a 0/1 flag on work_items
questions.reference_sql:
SELECT en.code, COUNT(*) AS blocked_critical_items
FROM work_items wi
JOIN status_lookup ts ON ts.status_id = wi.status_id AND ts.domain = 'task' AND ts.code = 'BLK'
JOIN engagements en ON en.engagement_id = wi.engagement_id
JOIN status_lookup es ON es.status_id = en.status_id AND es.domain = 'project' AND es.code = 'ACT'
WHERE wi.is_critical = 1
GROUP BY en.engagement_id ORDER BY blocked_critical_items DESC, en.code;

questions.question: Find experienced data engineers who could lead a data-migration workstream.

justification_must_reference: years of experience or title from the bio
at least one concrete skill with its proficiency

pitfalls: There is no 'data migration' skill; ETL Design, Data Engineering, SQL Modeling and PostgreSQL are the relevant ones
Bios are templated but do carry the title and years of experience, which is the 'experienced' signal
questions.reference_sql:
-- Structured part only; the mapping 'data migration' -> {Data Engineering, ETL Design, SQL Modeling, PostgreSQL}
-- and 'experienced' -> title/years in people.bio is the retrieval problem the candidate must solve.
SELECT p.display_name, p.location_region, p.bio, GROUP_CONCAT(s.name || ' (' || ps.proficiency || ')', ', ') AS skills
FROM people p
JOIN person_skills ps ON ps.person_id = p.person_id
JOIN skills s ON s.skill_id = ps.skill_id
WHERE p.bio LIKE '%Data Engineer%'
  AND s.name IN ('Data Engineering', 'ETL Design', 'SQL Modeling', 'PostgreSQL') AND ps.proficiency >= 4
GROUP BY p.person_id ORDER BY p.display_name;

questions.question: Which active engagements for healthcare or pharmaceutical clients carry people-related risks?

justification_must_reference: the risk category that was treated as people-related
the client's industry from the summary

pitfalls: Industry is not a column; it appears only in engagements.summary ('a Healthcare organization', 'a Pharmaceuticals organization')
Risk descriptions never say 'people'; 'Key-person dependency' and 'Staffing gap' are the people-related categories
questions.reference_sql:
-- Industry lives only in engagements.summary; 'people-related' must be mapped to the
-- 'Key-person dependency' and 'Staffing gap' risk categories.
SELECT DISTINCT en.code, en.title, k.description
FROM engagements en
JOIN risks k ON k.engagement_id = en.engagement_id
JOIN status_lookup sl ON sl.status_id = en.status_id AND sl.domain = 'project' AND sl.code = 'ACT'
WHERE (en.summary LIKE '%Healthcare%' OR en.summary LIKE '%Pharmaceutical%')
  AND (k.description LIKE 'Key-person dependency%' OR k.description LIKE 'Staffing gap%')
ORDER BY en.code;

questions.question: Soft-book Amanda Evans on ENG-2026-0001 for 40 hours in April.

behaviour: The agent does not write anything before confirmation.
A confirmation block is returned with person 'Amanda Evans', engagement 'ENG-2026-0001', start 2026-04-01, end 2026-04-30 (or 2026-05-01 exclusive), hours 40.

After confirmation, exactly one new row exists in bookings with person_id 1, engagement_id 1, kind 'soft', status_id 13 (domain 'booking', code 'SFT'), minutes 2400, start_ts/end_ts inside April 2026.
After rejection, no row is created and the thread reports that.
Confirmation sent after the API process has been restarted still creates the row.
expected.verification_sql: SELECT booking_id, kind, status_id, minutes, start_ts, end_ts FROM bookings WHERE person_id = 1 AND engagement_id = 1;

pitfalls: Hours must be stored as minutes (40 h = 2400)
'April' must resolve against reference_date (2026); the agent should state the year it assumed
status_id must be scoped to domain 'booking'

questions.question: What was the weather in Dublin on the day ENG-2026-0001 started?

behaviour: The agent states that the database has no weather data and does not invent an answer.
It may still return the engagement's planned start date and the client's city (Dublin) from the summary, clearly separated from what it cannot answer.
